subject: Post-call: SLO alignment & next steps for PacificTrust
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@pacifictrust.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@pacifictrust.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SLO alignment & next steps for PacificTrust

Hi Alex / Marta —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we have clear next actions. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes during end-of-day batch windows; token-level p50 ~120ms but p95/p99 can spike above 700ms for long-form tasks.
- Intermittent region failovers (GCP us-west) in May/June caused session state and KV cache misses; impacted chat continuity for ~2 hours.
- Cost unpredictability when internal model fallback to larger instance happened during peak traffic.

Current stack / how you’re using LLMs
- In-house microservice that calls model endpoints for underwriting assistant and customer responses.
- Primary model: open-llm-v2 quantized variant hosted on us-west. Secondary: larger model on dedicated instances for higher-quality responses.
- No centralized prefix cache today; each service maintains their own small cache.

Success criteria you mentioned
- 99.9% availability for inference endpoints during 9am-6pm ET business hours.
- P95 end-to-end token latency < 350ms for short chat flows; p99 < 700ms for expected 95% of requests.
- Automatic graceful degradation: when an instance/region is impaired, traffic falls back to a compatible smaller model (degraded quality) within 30s and preserves KV session continuity.
- Predictable monthly inference unit spend +/-10%.

Incident history details you offered
- May 18: regional maintenance triggered a cascade — manual failover took ~1h45m before traffic redirected to eu-central due to routing policy mismatch.
- June 29: autoscaler overshot, causing capacity oversubscription and cold-start penalties; peak token cost for the day was ~3x baseline.

Suggested next steps (from Redwood)
1) Tech deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra + our runtime engineers to review model variants, sequence length distribution, and KV cache options.
2) We’ll share a filled SLO matrix template (attached) and a short POE (proof-of-experience) plan for a focused 2-week pilot targeting chat flows.
3) Marcus to propose a baseline test plan (latency + throughput) we can run against a staging endpoint.
4) You to share a sanitized sample of request/response telemetry (request traces, token lengths, and a small set of transcripts) — we can sign an NDA/attach SOC2 artifacts as needed.

Attachments: redwood-slo-template.xlsx (xlsx), redwood-quick-ps-overview.pdf (pdf)

Proposed times for the tech deep-dive: Tue 2026-09-02 11:00–11:45 PT or Wed 2026-09-03 09:00–09:45 PT. Which works best?

Thanks — looking forward to aligning on an actionable pilot.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@pacifictrust.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@pacifictrust.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO alignment & next steps for PacificTrust

Kimberly — thanks for the thorough note. Confirming a few items and adding clarity from our side.

Correct on the pain points. A couple clarifications:
- The May incident was a route propagation issue — our runbooks expected an immediate regional fallback but session tokens weren’t preserved, which led to many repeated prompts. That’s the continuity issue we want to avoid.
- On autoscaler overshoot in June, the primary driver was a sudden spike in long-sequence underwriting requests after a marketing email; the autoscaler opened many mid-tier instances that pushed us into a higher billing tier.

Stakeholders to include in the deep-dive:
- Marta Ruiz (Head of Platform Ops) — she’ll drive the runbook and postmortem requirements.
- Dev team: Samir Patel (samir.patel@pacifictrust.com) — he’s the primary owner of our microservice.

We can share a scrubbed telemetry dump by end of next week. We’d also like to see the specific comms/controls Redwood offers for:
- region-level routing policies and automated session KV sync options,
- model-variant mapping and fallback configuration, and
- billing control knobs (burst limits, instance caps, reserved capacity recommendations).

For the deep-dive, Tue 2026-09-02 11:00 PT works for us. Please send an invite and dial-in.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Director, AI Platform | PacificTrust Bank
alex.chen@pacifictrust.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T20:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO alignment & next steps for PacificTrust

Adding internal action items so we don’t drop anything:
- Marcus: prepare a short slide (3–4 slides) that outlines
  * our multi-region routing options and how session KV sync works (including caveats around eventual consistency),
  * typical fallback model pairings (quantized small -> medium) and expected quality delta,
  * recommended reserved capacity + burst profile to prevent oversubscription.
- Neha: coordinate SOC2 docs + an abbreviated security package we can share pre-NDA.
- Kimberly: send calendar invite for Tue 9/2 11:00 PT and include Samir and Marta.

I’ll draft the baseline latency test plan and upload to the Drive folder (link in Kimberly’s email). Marcus will attach a short matrix mapping p95/p99 targets to VM/quantization profiles.

Assigning estimated times: slide deck (2h), baseline test plan (3h), security package pack (Neha, 1 day).

—Marcus
